tb-208-5.question:
Two objects, P and Q, are projected from the same level at the same time. P is projected vertically upwards at a speed of 30 m s−1 while Q is projected at an angle of 60° to the vertical at a speed of 60 m s−1 (Fig d). The objects land on positions at the same level.

(2) P and Q have the same acceleration throughout their flights.

(3) P and Q are momentarily at rest when they reach their maximum height.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-208-5.reasoning:
The acceleration is 9.81 m s–2 (downwards) for both P and Q.

∴ (2) is correct.

Initial vertical speed of Q

= 60 cos 60° = 30 m s–1

Since P and Q have the same initial vertical speed, their time of flight are the same.

tb-208-6.question:
Objects X and Y are projected from the same position P and land at the same position Q. X is projected at an angle below the horizontal while Y is projected horizontally. Which of the following statements about the objects is/are correct?

(1) They have the same time of flight.

(2) They have the same landing speed.

(3) They have different initial horizontal speeds.

A (3) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-208-6.reasoning:
The initial velocity of X has a downward component while the initial vertical speed of Y is zero. Therefore, the time of flight of X is shorter than that of Y.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

As they have the same range and the time of flight of X is shorter than that of Y, the initial horizontal speed of X is greater than that of Y.

∴ (3) is correct.

As Y has a zero initial vertical speed and a smaller initial horizontal speed than X, Y has a smaller initial speed than X. By the law of conservation of energy, it has a smaller landing speed than X.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

tb-208-11.question:
A ball is released from rest at point X on a smooth track (Fig i). It undergoes projectile motion after leaving the track at Y, and eventually falls onto the horizontal ground.

Which of the following statements about the projectile motion of the ball must be correct?

(1) The maximum height reached by the ball is lower than X.

(2) The ball’s range is related to its angle of projection at Y.

(3) The ball’s speed when it hits the ground is related to its angle of projection at Y.

A (2) only

B (1) and (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-208-11.reasoning:
The KE of the ball at the maximum height reached by the ball is not zero as it has a constant horizontal speed during the projectile motion. By the law of conservation of energy, its PE at the maximum height must be smaller than that at X. Therefore, the maximum height reached by the ball must be lower than X.

∴ (1) is correct.

The range of the projectile motion depends on the angle of projection.

∴ (2) is correct.

By the law of conservation of energy, the ball’s speed when it hits the ground depends on the height of Y and the speed of the ball at Y, but not the angle of projection at Y.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-208-26.question:
A spring gun is installed on a cart which moves with a constant velocity on a smooth horizontal track. The gun points vertically upwards and fires a ball at a certain instant (Fig z).

(a) Does the ball fall back onto the cart? Explain briefly. (2 marks)

(b) How will the time of flight and range of the ball change if

(i) the cart moves faster;

(ii) the ball is launched at a higher speed? (4 marks)

(c) The cart is now pulled by a constant force (Fig aa). Can the ball fall back onto the cart after it is fired? Explain briefly. (3 marks)
tb-208-26.answer:
(a) Yes. 1A

The ball and the cart have the same horizontal velocity. Therefore, they would have travelled the same horizontal distance in the same period of time. 1A

(b) (i) The time of flight will be unchanged. 1A

The range will increase. 1A

(ii) The time of flight will increase. 1A

The range will increase. 1A

(c) No. 1A

After the ball leaves the cart, its horizontal velocity is constant. 1A

However, the cart will move horizontally with a constant acceleration as there is a constant net force acting on it. 1A
